title: Kerala Steps In to Bring Home Seafarer Stranded in Iran After Pakistan Seizes Crew's Documents
excerpt: Kollam native Akshay Harish has spent nearly a month confined in Chabahar after his ship's documents were confiscated in Pakistan and lost; the Indian Embassy in Iran is expected to issue him temporary travel papers.
body:
• Akshay Harish, a seafarer from Prakkulam in Kollam, has been stranded in Chabahar, Iran, for nearly a month after Pakistani port authorities seized the passports and Continuous Discharge Certificates of his ship's crew and the documents were never returned.
  • His vessel, the Palm Marine, ran into fines and certificate problems in Pakistan; after the penalties were paid and the ship returned to Iran, the crew's passports and CDCs went missing from the captain's custody.
  • Six Myanmar nationals aboard were repatriated through their embassy, but Akshay was left behind, confined to a room in Chabahar without travel documents.
  • Kerala's government has intervened: the state's labour minister and Union Minister Suresh Gopi have taken the case up with the Chief Minister, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, and the Indian Embassy in Iran, which is expected to meet Akshay and issue temporary travel documents.

The Kerala government has stepped in to bring home a young seafarer from Kollam who has been stranded in Iran without a passport after Pakistani port authorities seized his travel documents and never returned them. Akshay Harish, a native of Prakkulam in Kollam district, is confined to a room in the port city of Chabahar, according to The Hindu, which reported that Pakistani authorities seized and failed to return the passports and Continuous Discharge Certificates (CDCs) of crew members, including Akshay, aboard the Dubai- and Iran-owned vessel Palm Marine.

How He Got Stranded

Akshay joined the shipping company on December 5, 2025, through a recruiting agency based in Palakkad, initially boarding a ship from Japan, ANI reported. As the regional war intensified, the vessel could not travel from Iran to Dubai or Oman and instead sailed from Iran to Pakistan carrying rice. The first voyage went smoothly; on the second, Pakistani port authorities confiscated the passports and CDCs of the cabin crew, chief engineer, and captain, citing problems with the captain's certificates and imposing heavy fines.

The penalties were paid and the ship returned to Iran — but the passports and travel documents went missing from the captain's custody. The crew then sat aboard the ship at the port for nearly a month. The Iranian captain and chief engineer eventually departed, and six Myanmar nationals aboard were repatriated through their embassy. Akshay was left behind in Chabahar, where he says his paperwork has still not been cleared and could take months.

"Please save me somehow."

— Akshay Harish, seafarer from Kollam, in his appeal from Chabahar

The Rescue Effort

Kerala's labour minister has written to the Chief Minister, Union External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Kerala's Special Representative in Delhi, and the Indian Embassy in Iran, ANI reported, and Union Minister Suresh Gopi has also taken up the case. The matter has been formally raised with the Iranian Ambassador, and officials from the Indian Embassy are slated to meet Akshay in person to issue temporary travel documents — the step that would let him fly home despite the missing passport. For the thousands of Malayali seafarers working foreign-flag vessels, the case is a reminder of how quickly a documents dispute abroad can leave a crew member stateless in practice: without a passport or CDC, Akshay cannot board a ship or a flight, and only consular intervention can cut through it.
